title: How Political Advertising Will Impact the Media Landscape in 2026

facts.fact: AdImpact projects 2026 US midterm political ad spending to reach $10.8 billion, a 20%-plus increase over the 2022 midterms' $8.9 billion.
facts.quote: Political ad spending this cycle is projected to reach [$10.8 billion](https://adimpact.com/political-projections-26), a 20%-plus increase over the 2022 midterms’ $8.9 billion

facts.fact: Political CTV ad spending is projected to reach $2.4 billion in 2026 according to AdImpact.
facts.quote: Political CTV spending is projected to reach [$2.4 billion](https://adimpact.com/political-projections-26) in 2026

facts.fact: California is projected to lead all states in 2026 political ad spending at $1.1 billion, per AdImpact.
facts.quote: California is projected to lead all states at $1.1 billion in political spending

facts.fact: Senate political ad spending in 2026 is projected at $2.8 billion, per AdImpact.
facts.quote: spending is projected to hit [$2.8 billion](https://adimpact.com/political-projections-26), slightly surpassing the 2024 record.

facts.fact: House political ad spending in 2026 is projected at $2.2 billion, per AdImpact.
facts.quote: Spending on House races, on the other hand, is projected to reach [$2.2 billion](https://adimpact.com/political-projections-26)

facts.fact: Gubernatorial political ad spending in 2026 is expected to hit $1.95 billion, per AdImpact.
facts.quote: Gubernatorial spending is expected to hit [$1.95 billion](https://adimpact.com/political-projections-26)

facts.fact: Downballot political spending is projected to account for 36% of all 2026 political ad spending, representing $3.9 billion.
facts.quote: downballot spending, driven by ballot propositions and state legislative races, will account for 36% of all political ad spending, representing $3.9 billion.

facts.fact: Total US political ad spending in the 2024 cycle was $11.2 billion, with the presidential race accounting for $3.2 billion.
facts.quote: During the 2024 election cycle, political ad spending totaled [$11.2 billion](https://adimpact.com/political-projections-26), with the presidential race alone accounting for $3.2 billion.

facts.fact: The 2026 midterms include 35 Senate seats in play, including special elections in Florida and Ohio.
facts.quote: with [35 Senate seats](https://bipartisanpolicy.org/article/the-2026-midterms-key-dates-and-events/) in play, including special elections in Florida and Ohio.

facts.fact: All 435 House seats will be contested in the 2026 midterm elections.
facts.quote: All 435 House seats will be contested

facts.fact: Basis states that 12 of the projected 40 competitive House seats sit in the New York and Los Angeles metropolitan areas.
facts.quote: 12 of the projected 40 competitive seats sit in those two metropolitan areas

facts.fact: The Senate currently has a 53-47 Republican majority, against which Democrats are pursuing pickup opportunities.
facts.quote: Democrats pursue pickup opportunities against a 53-47 Republican majority

facts.fact: Downballot political spending in 2026 is projected at 36% of all political ad spending, per Basis.
facts.quote: will account for 36% of all political ad spending

facts.quote: California ($1.1 billion), Michigan ($936 million), Georgia ($757 million), North Carolina ($669 million), and Texas ($556 million)

facts.quote: Michigan ($936 million)

facts.quote: Georgia ($757 million)

facts.fact: Streaming captured 47.5% of all TV viewing in December 2025, according to Nielsen's The Gauge.
facts.quote: Streaming captured 47.5% of all TV viewing in December 2025

facts.fact: Major CTV platforms Netflix and Amazon Prime Video do not currently accept political advertising.
facts.quote: Major CTV platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video do not currently accept political advertising

facts.fact: There is no federal law governing the widespread use of AI in political advertising.
facts.quote: There is no federal law governing the widespread use of AI in political advertising

facts.fact: The National Republican Senatorial Committee released an 85-second deepfake video of Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico in March 2026.
facts.quote: released an 85-second deepfake video of James Talarico

facts.fact: Political ad spending for the cycle is described as a $10.8 billion political advertising cycle.
facts.quote: Navigating a $10.8 billion political advertising cycle

facts.fact: The peak political ad spending window runs from Labor Day through Election Day, when college football and the NFL overlap with political spending.
facts.quote: from Labor Day through Election Day, college football and the NFL will overlap directly with peak political ad spending

facts.fact: The 2026 midterms will test nonpolitical advertisers' ability to maintain reach and performance in a historically expensive and complex media environment, according to Basis.
facts.quote: The 2026 midterms will test nonpolitical advertisers' ability to maintain reach and performance in a historically expensive and complex media environment.

facts.fact: Basis says a record amount of political spending is projected to flood broadcast TV, CTV, and digital channels in the 2026 cycle.
facts.quote: With a record amount of political spending projected to flood broadcast TV, CTV, and digital channels

facts.fact: Basis says the pressure on nonpolitical advertisers will be acute in battleground states and high-profile metropolitan areas from Labor Day through Election Day.
facts.quote: the pressure will be acute in battleground states and high-profile metropolitan areas from Labor Day through Election Day.

facts.fact: Basis states that waiting until September will likely mean paying peak prices or being shut out of premium CTV and video inventory, which it expects to be the most contested.
facts.quote: waiting until September will likely mean paying peak prices—or being shut out entirely.

facts.fact: Basis states that November through December historically offers favorable pricing as political dollars exit the market.
facts.quote: November through December historically offers favorable pricing as political dollars exit the market.

facts.fact: Basis recommends tapering advertising in the weeks before Election Day, when it says CPMs peak, and accelerating in the November-through-December window, when it says pricing typically drops.
facts.quote: tapering in the weeks before Election Day when CPMs peak and accelerating in the November-through-December window when political dollars exit and pricing typically drops.

facts.fact: Basis says block lists and keyword exclusions set in Q1 may not reflect the political content environment by September, so mid-cycle reviews are advised.
facts.quote: Block lists and keyword exclusions set in Q1 may not reflect the political content environment by September.

facts.fact: Basis says adjacency risks are highest for display and online video, so brand safety placement quality should be reviewed there.
facts.quote: particularly for display and online video, where adjacency risks are highest.

facts.fact: Basis says CPMs can spike on platforms that accept political ads, so advertisers should earmark budget for reallocation to less contested channels.
facts.quote: When CPMs spike on platforms that accept political ads, having budget earmarked for reallocation gives advertisers room to move.

facts.fact: Basis states that programmatic guaranteed and private marketplace deals can lock in pricing and access before the market tightens in Q3 and Q4.
facts.quote: programmatic guaranteed (PG) deals and private marketplace (PMP) arrangements offer a way to lock in pricing and access before the market tightens.
